thesis: Low valuation and weak growth coexist with higher provisioning. The debate turns on capital and payout information neither side supplies.
strongest_counterexample: An 8.36x earnings multiple plus positive H1 profit despite higher impairments could already compensate for conservative growth.
invalidation_conditions: Analyst-selected review rule, not a sourced forecast: reassess this ruling if two consecutive quarters of falling year-on-year attributable profit.

Analyst-selected review rule, not a sourced forecast: reassess this ruling if two consecutive quarters of positive year-on-year attributable profit growth with impairment-charge growth below revenue growth.
evidence_gaps: Capital ratios, credit-cost history and payout coverage.
Underlying statement periods and forward-estimate dates are not fully supplied.
decisive_factors: Low headline valuation and modest positive earnings support a possible value case
Resilient half-year profit deserves credit, yet higher provisioning and unverified annual payout remain the decisive combination
